definition: Yellowbrick draws diagnostic plots for scikit-learn models — confusion matrices, ROC curves, learning curves, elbow plots.
details: Created by Benjamin Bengfort and Rebecca Bilbro (District Data Labs) in 2016.

explainer.lead: How to install Yellowbrick, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

quickstart.python:
from sklearn.datasets import load_breast_cancer
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from yellowbrick.classifier import ConfusionMatrix

X, y = load_breast_cancer(return_X_y=True)
viz = ConfusionMatrix(LogisticRegression(max_iter=5000))
viz.fit(X, y)
viz.score(X, y)
viz.show()

explainer.inAi: See where a classifier goes wrong before you reach for a bigger model.
explainer.jsNote: Yellowbrick is a Python library with no official JavaScript or TypeScript package; call it from a Python service if your app is written in JavaScript.

tiers.eli5: It is a box of ready-made charts that shows how well your model is doing, like a dashboard for a car you built.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers wrap a scikit-learn estimator in a Yellowbrick visualiser and call fit to get a plot for tuning or reporting. A common pitfall is treating a good-looking plot as validation without checking it on held-out data.
tiers.paperLevel: Yellowbrick provides visualisers for scikit-learn models; it reports diagnostics rather than defining new metrics, so its value is bound by the underlying scikit-learn evaluation measures.

explainer.example: Wrap a classifier in a ROC curve visualiser, fit it on training data, and read the resulting curve to compare thresholds before choosing one.
